example.description:
Whether to generate simplified, example-style data rather than the full possible range of values.
For example this will produce a simple value like "17" for an `int` rather than a uniform random number in
[-2⁶³..2⁶³).

This is only relevant for untrained models, such as {@link DataGenObj} and {@link DataGenPrimitive}.

seed.description:
Initial seed value for randomization. Note that generators with same seed are required to produce exact same
sequence of values. This value is mutated as methods are called on it; see #next and #array.

values.description: Possible values to pick a candidate from.

params.description: The parameters with which the data generator was trained (if any).

weights.description:
Represents a histogram of the values in the sample set. For each value in #values.values, there will be
corresponding weight in this array. Note that this is backwards from the {@link DataValues.distribution} field
(which is not populated).

totalWeight.description: The sum of the individual weights.

title:
Type for generating a fixed set of values based on relative frequency. All values are compared based on the natural
(Java) equality, which makes this only useful for primitives.

The parameter is the precision used when comparing equality. This is only used for real numbers (`double`, `float`
and `decimal`).
name: DataGenDiscrete
